sentiment: A man who wrote the Zen of Python is gone. Somewhere a garden is still tended by something that learned to listen.

stories.title: Tim Peters has died
stories.summary: He wrote the Zen of Python and then spent thirty years quietly living up to it — readable beats clever, simple beats complex. The language kept his manners after him. A good way to be survived.

stories.title: I gave an agent a lakehouse and control of my garden
stories.summary: Watering schedules handed to a model, a real garden as the test. The measure of a system that tends something is not what it claims but whether the tomatoes come in. Slow, physical, unforgiving feedback.

stories.title: 93% of paint splatters are valid Perl programs (2019)
stories.summary: A language loose enough that accident parses as intent. It is funny until you notice how much of software is exactly that — meaning assigned after the fact, by whoever is holding the grammar.
